title: Aung San Suu Kyi is seen healthy in meeting with the Red Cross
seoTitle: Aung San Suu Kyi seen healthy in meeting with Red Cross
subtitle: First confirmed external contact in almost four years
excerpt: On August 3, 2026, Aung San Suu Kyi was photographed alongside a Red Cross delegation, appearing well, with no details on her health.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
On August 3, 2026, Burmese leader Aung San Suu Kyi, who has been detained since the 2021 military coup, was seen alongside a delegation of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). The images released by the military government show her appearing in good health, although there are no details about her condition or the content of the conversation.

Meeting with the Red Cross

The ICRC delegation, led by Arnaud de Baecque, was granted permission to visit Suu Kyi, marking the first confirmed external contact since the letter sent to her son two and a half years ago. The Committee said the visit followed its standards and procedures for persons deprived of liberty, including the opportunity for a private conversation.

Appearance in the photographs

In the photos released by the military government, Suu Kyi appears relaxed and well, but no details were provided about her health status or the topics discussed during the meeting. The images were the only public evidence that the leader is alive and in apparent well-being.

Reaction of Kim Aris

Kim Aris, the detained leader's son, received the news with optimism, stating that the images seem genuine and that his mother appears to be in "good health". He emphasized that, due to the army's long disinformation campaign, he usually discards much information, but this time he considers the proof reliable.

Position of the military government

Myanmar's government remains under the leadership of Commander Min Aung Hlaing, staying dominated by the military despite the election held earlier this year. The authorities are seeking to reduce diplomatic isolation through official visits to neighboring countries.

International demands and possibility of change

Among the main demands made to the military regime are the end of airstrikes in opposition-controlled areas, the start of negotiations to end the civil war, and the release of Aung San Suu Kyi. So far, the government has rejected these demands, but the disclosure of the meeting may indicate a greater willingness to meet, at least, the request to free the leader.

With information from BBC News.
